title: A new 3D-printed solution significantly reduces energy consumption for cooling in data centers
summary: AM2PC project: DTI and Heatflow, with Open Engineering and Fraunhofer IWU, built and tested a 3D-printed aluminium passive two-phase evaporator for data centres and HPC with no pumps or fans. Tested at 600 W, 50% above the 400 W target. Rejects heat at 60-80 C, usable for district heating. LCA indicates 25-30% lower emissions per unit. Demonstration project.
thermal: Passive two-phase thermosiphon evaporator, 600 W tested, no pumps or fans.
manufacturing: Single-piece aluminium part made by laser powder bed fusion to remove joints and leak paths.

title: Danish researchers develop 3D-printed vapor chamber for two-phase liquid cooling
summary: Same AM2PC story as the DTI release. Confirms the vapour chamber was made by laser powder bed fusion (PBF-LB) and that Heatflow is a Danish two-phase electronics cooling firm founded in 2018.
thermal: Passive two-phase evaporator, 600 W.

title: This startup's metal stacks could help solve AI's massive heat problem
summary: Alloy Enterprises makes copper cold plates by 'stack forging': laser-cut copper sheets stacked and diffusion bonded into seamless plates with features down to 50 microns, for GPUs and for memory and networking chips (about 20% of server cooling load). Claims 35% better thermal performance than competitors, at a cost between machining and 3D printing. Context: Nvidia Rubin Ultra racks expected to draw up to 600 kW in 2027.
thermal: Seamless copper cold plates with 50 micron internal channels.
manufacturing: Laser cutting plus diffusion bonding of stacked sheets; an alternative to AM and machining.

title: 3D printing cold plates for AI datacentre cooling
summary: Fabric8Labs' electrochemical additive manufacturing (ECAM) prints copper fin and micro-mesh boiling structures at room temperature with 33 micron resolution, directly onto PCBs or silicon. Claims 48% better thermal performance than microchannels. Wiwynn uses it for a 3.5 kW cold plate; AEWIN for boiling plates on networking gear. Backed by Intel Capital, TDK Ventures and Schneider Electric.
thermal: Hot-spot-targeted copper fins and micro-mesh boiling surfaces.
manufacturing: Electrochemical AM of copper, optimised to the chip power map.

title: Microfluidics Could Be the Answer to Cooling AI Chips
summary: Swiss firm Corintis designs microfluidic copper cold plates with about 70 micron channels using its own simulation and optimisation software. In a Microsoft test, heat removal was three times as efficient as existing methods and chip temperatures fell more than 80% versus air. Over 10,000 cold plates made, target one million by end of 2026; US$24m Series A. Etching channels into the chip itself is at prototype stage.
thermal: Microfluidic cold plates routing coolant to hot spots.
manufacturing: Simulation-driven channel design; AM for volume production of copper cold plates.

title: Generative Design for Direct-to-Chip Liquid Cooling for Data Centers
summary: Preprint from the University of Michigan-Dearborn. A reaction-diffusion generative design loop coupled to a finite-difference thermal model synthesises cold-plate channels for the Nvidia GB200 superchip. Simulated: more than 5 C lower average and over 35 C lower maximum temperature than a parallel-channel baseline. No fabrication or test.
thermal: Generative cold-plate channel layouts that remove hot spots.
manufacturing: Design and modelling only; the geometries would need AM or fine machining to make.

title: Iceotope passes 200 patents as AI cooling demand rises
summary: Iceotope has over 200 liquid-cooling patents (109 granted). Its sealed-chassis 'precision liquid cooling' uses a small amount of dielectric fluid to cool all server components. Claims up to 40% lower energy and 96% lower water use than traditional cooling. Cites a $40-45bn data-centre cooling market by 2030.
thermal: Sealed-server dielectric liquid cooling combining direct-to-chip and immersion features.
manufacturing: Chassis and fluid-path design; no process detail.

title: Why AI Data Centres Should Think More Like Formula One Teams
summary: Conflux argues data-centre cooling should be engineered as a system, weighing thermal resistance against pressure drop because pump energy adds up over thousands of servers. Cites its single-phase AM cold plates at 0.0076 C/W at 6 L/min over 2,500 mm2 with low pressure drop. Opinion piece by a former F1 engineer; one vendor data point.
thermal: Joint optimisation of cold-plate thermal resistance and pressure drop.
manufacturing: CFD-designed monolithic AM cold plates; in-house calorimetric and rack-scale testing.

title: What motorsport can teach data centres about thermal management
summary: Syndicated version of the Conflux op-ed by Executive Chairman Michael Fuller: judge liquid cooling by total energy including pump work, not heat removal alone. Same 0.0076 C/W cold-plate figure.
thermal: Cold plates optimised for thermal resistance and pressure drop together.

title: Conflux Technology Expands with New UK Business Hub
summary: Conflux, the Australian AM heat-exchanger developer, is opening a UK hub to serve Europe (over 35% of its business). It starts with R&D, materials certification and supply-chain support, with plans to scale to production. European partners include several Formula 1 teams.
thermal: AM heat exchangers for aerospace, automotive, energy and defence.
manufacturing: Conflux Production System: thermo-fluid design plus metal AM; UK hub does materials certification.

title: Bradford approves Deep Green data centre heat reuse
summary: Deep Green has planning approval for a 5.6 MW heat-reusing AI/HPC data centre in Bradford feeding the 1Energy district heat network. Claims no water use, up to 95% heat reuse and over 4,500 t CO2 a year saved. Planning stage.
thermal: Closed-loop waterless cooling with heat exported to district heating.

title: UK government reveals £90m plan to warm homes with data center waste heat
summary: DESNZ is funding £90m of heat networks to carry data-centre heat to about 750,000 homes: £41m for London's mega heat project, £9.7m for Bradford, plus Greater Manchester, Newport, Abergavenny and Solihull. Electric barges will carry hot water 25 km along the Thames from 2028.

orgs.name: Department for Energy Security and Net Zero

thermal: Data-centre waste heat delivered as hot water through heat networks.

title: Waste heat from UK data centres could heat 3.5m+ homes
summary: EnergiRaven and Viegand Maagøe estimate UK data centres could heat 3.5m to 6.3m homes by 2035 depending on design, proposing Greater Manchester as a pilot and calling for strategic 'Heat Highways'. Modelled projection.
thermal: Data-centre waste heat recovery into heat networks.

title: Next Generation Green Data Centres
summary: Innovate UK project (2016-2019, £2.5m) led by Heriot-Watt with Universiti Teknologi Malaysia and Dearman, targeting a 50% energy cut through new cooling, waste-heat recovery and liquid-nitrogen cold-energy capture. Older work, useful as UK research history.
thermal: Data-centre cooling, waste heat recovery and cold storage.

title: CoolHeatDC - Two-phase immersion cooling with integrated heat upgrade in data centres
summary: SINTEF project combining two-phase immersion cooling with a directly coupled heat pump using natural refrigerants, to upgrade server heat for district and industrial heating at hyperscale (over 50 MW). Lab-scale testing plus design and techno-economic modelling. No results yet.
thermal: Two-phase immersion cooling integrated with heat-pump upgrade.
manufacturing: Modelling and simulation tools; no manufacturing.

title: Hot Chips
summary: UKPN Strategic Innovation Fund discovery project (£149k, May-Jul 2025) on reusing data-centre heat in 4th and 5th generation district heating, lifting 25-40 C heat to 55-60 C with water-source heat pumps. Cites NESO: 35 TWh of data-centre electricity by 2050, about 40% for cooling.
thermal: Low-grade data-centre heat upgraded by heat pumps.

title: ZutaCore secures $100m Series C funding to push liquid cooling tech
summary: ZutaCore raised $100m from Mitsubishi Electric, Carrier Ventures and Samsung for its waterless direct-to-chip two-phase cooling, designed for processors above 4,000 W and deployed in over 75 sites.
thermal: Direct-to-chip two-phase boiling cooling above 4 kW per chip.

title: UK Heatwave Disrupts Cambridge AI Supercomputer and Research Workloads
summary: Cambridge's Dawn AI supercomputer went offline with 'technical problems' during the late-June 2026 UK heatwave (37.3 C June record). The article urges buyers to ask about cooling limits and ambient thresholds; the cause is not confirmed as thermal.
thermal: Heat resilience of dense AI/HPC facilities in UK heatwaves.

title: Meggitt secures £3.7m thermal management development grant
summary: ATI grant, matched by the consortium, funds a £7.4m programme on lighter, more compact heat exchangers for next-generation passenger aero engines, made at Meggitt's Midlands Thermal Management Centre of Excellence. Partners: AMRC, AFRC, MTC, S&C Thermal Fluids and Cranfield.
thermal: Compact lightweight aero-engine heat exchangers.
manufacturing: Manufacturing development with HVM Catapult centres; process not named.

title: Meggitt announces investment in HiETA Technologies
summary: Meggitt invested in Bristol-based HiETA Technologies, a UK metal AM specialist, to accelerate next-generation lightweight thermal systems for aerospace and energy, combining Meggitt's heat-exchanger experience with HiETA's AM design.
thermal: Lightweight high-performance aerospace thermal systems.

title: Additive Manufacturing for Aerospace Heat Exchangers
summary: TWI, University of Birmingham and Meggitt published a review in Applied Thermal Engineering on L-PBF heat exchangers for aerospace, focusing on aluminium alloys. Part of the Clean Sky 2 C-ALM AOHE project (compact additive layer manufactured air-oil heat exchanger, grant 831880).
thermal: Air-oil heat exchangers for aero engines.
manufacturing: Laser powder bed fusion of aluminium heat exchangers.

title: Promising results for heat exchangers on hydrogen aircraft
summary: Chalmers and GKN Aerospace (patent filed) use cryogenic hydrogen to cool engine parts and exhaust heat to preheat fuel. Reported almost 8% lower take-off fuel burn and 37% lower NOx for short/medium-range aircraft, potentially 10% more range. From EU ENABLEH2 and PATH projects.
thermal: Compact heat exchangers for hydrogen engine intercooling and recuperation.
manufacturing: Design and testing; process not stated.

title: HEX 4 ELECTRA
summary: DLR's Institute of Electrified Aero Engines is developing 3D-printed TPMS heat exchangers with integrated coolant channels for fuel-cell aircraft, where thermal management can be a large share of propulsion weight and volume. Validated at TRL 4 in lab tests at BTU Cottbus; larger tests planned.

orgs.name: DLR Institute of Electrified Aero Engines

thermal: TPMS compact heat exchangers for fuel-cell propulsion.
manufacturing: AM of TPMS structures, validated on a modular air-duct test rig.

title: Why Mercedes' Hywel Thomas claims the sport faces its greatest engineering challenge
summary: Mercedes AMG HPP's managing director calls the 2026 rules a revolution: MGU-H removed, MGU-K up from 120 kW to 350 kW, near-equal ICE/electric split, sustainable fuel. Battery, MGU-K and turbo run harder while chassis rules cut downforce and cooling airflow, so cooling must be built into the aero concept from the start.
thermal: Higher electrical heat loads with less cooling airflow.
manufacturing: More simulation and faster design-validate loops.

title: Off the Grid: Why F1's Thermal Limits Demand Simulation Flexibility
summary: Vendor blog: in 2026 electrical power rises to about 350 kW while ICE falls to about 400 kW; active aero makes duct flow transient. Proposes non-rectangular heat exchangers, CFD-to-1D mapping and transient system models; notes 3D-printed metal cores as a trend.
thermal: Battery, MGU-K and intercooler heat rejection under transient airflow.
manufacturing: System modelling of heat exchangers; mentions AM cores.

title: Evaluation of thermal performance of the MGU-K for 2026 F1 power unit regulations
summary: Oxford Brookes paper (Bayram and Samuel) models the MGU-K under 2024 and 2026 rules with GT-Drive, validated on 2023 qualifying data, and feeds heat losses to a lumped-parameter plus FEA thermal model to predict temperature rise and propose cooling specifications.
thermal: MGU-K heat generation and cooling specification for 2026.

title: F1 tightens 2026 rules to close off tyre cooling tricks
summary: FIA bans devices that heat, cool or maintain the temperature of wheels, hubs or brakes, and requires sealed suspension fairings. Regulatory change, no technology.
thermal: Wheel and brake temperature regulation.

title: How F1 teams have adapted their cars for Mexico's cooling headache
summary: At the Mexico GP (2,200 m, about 20% lower air density) most teams brought cooling-only parts: bigger louvres, revised engine covers and larger brake-duct scoops. No data.
thermal: Cooling at altitude: louvres, exits, brake ducts.

title: F1 2026 sidepods: Radical Audi F1 solution, Red Bull makes early RB22 change
summary: Visual analysis of 2026 sidepods: Audi's narrow vertical inlet, Red Bull's switch to a full ramp, Alpine's swappable midsection panel for cooling gills, Aston Martin's tight wrap around the heat exchangers.
thermal: Heat-exchanger packaging and inlet design.

title: How the Cadillac Formula 1 Team makes a brake duct
summary: Cadillac F1 explains brake-duct design: discs exceed 700 C, ducts are shaped to FIA rules and cooling needs, and the team 3D-prints prototypes to check simulation predictions.
thermal: Brake cooling airflow.

title: Formula 1 approves Aheadd CP1 aluminium for additively manufactured heat exchangers
summary: Constellium's Aheadd CP1 Al-Fe-Zr alloy for L-PBF is approved for F1. Constellium, Velo3D and PWR supply AM heat exchangers from the 2024 season. Thermally stable to 300 C; qualified at 50 and 100 micron layers.
thermal: Compact lightweight AM heat exchangers for F1.
manufacturing: L-PBF with PWR brazed-fin technology; new parameter sets.

title: PWR and Eplus3D partnership brings advanced cooling solutions through Additive Manufacturing
summary: Eplus3D case study: PWR chose Eplus3D after a multi-vendor test; parameters for Aheadd CP1 reach 99.93% density with leak-tight thin tube walls and fine fins.
thermal: Thin-wall AM heat exchangers.
manufacturing: L-PBF parameter development for a heat-exchanger alloy.

title: PWR Advanced Cooling Technology Chooses Velo3D to Print Heat Exchangers
summary: 2019 partnership: PWR and Velo3D to develop aluminium alloys and serial AM production of thin-wall heat exchangers for motorsport, batteries, electronics and aerospace.
thermal: Thin-wall heat exchangers where weight and pressure drop matter.

title: Multimatic Motorsports proves reliability of 3D printed thermal systems on the track
summary: A Conflux AM transmission oil cooler, built on its configurable core platform in two weeks, completed a full endurance race on a Multimatic car. Reported about 20% more heat rejection than the incumbent in the same envelope with no added weight.
thermal: Liquid-liquid transmission oil cooler, +20% heat rejection.

title: Conflux Technology and Dallara collaborate on 3D printed heat exchangers
summary: Conflux and Dallara to develop small AM heat exchangers for motorsport meeting tight performance, quality and cost targets.
thermal: Small motorsport heat exchangers.

title: Additive manufacturing material from HRL Laboratories approved for Formula 1 use
summary: HRL's 7A77 high-strength AM aluminium alloy approved by the FIA for any F1 component.
thermal: none
gate_reason: Structural alloy news with no thermal content.

title: Roboze supports F1 composite brake cooling duct manufacture
summary: Visa Cash App RB prints brake cooling ducts in carbon-fibre PEEK on Roboze machines; reports 68% faster production and 66% shorter lead time.
thermal: Brake cooling ducts.
manufacturing: Polymer composite AM replacing moulded ducts.

title: Williams Advanced Engineering to provide next-generation battery for Formula E
summary: WAE wins the Formula E Gen3 battery contract. Only passing mention of thermal efficiency.
thermal: Passing mention only.
gate_reason: Supply contract news with no thermal content.

title: 3D printed parts to improve McLaren F1 performance
summary: 2017: McLaren used Stratasys printing for brackets, tooling and soluble cores for composite brake cooling ducts. Old and mostly non-thermal.
thermal: Brake cooling ducts via soluble cores.
gate_reason: Mostly non-thermal parts; 2017.

title: Thermal Management Roadmap Report (FZO-PPN-COM-0019)
summary: FlyZero heat-exchanger roadmap for liquid-hydrogen aircraft (gas turbine and fuel cell). Fuel-cell air radiators are the biggest thermal challenge (megawatt heat loads at low temperature difference while LT-PEM stacks run at 80 C). Targets for fuel-cell thermal management specific heat rejection: 5 kW/kg (2026), 10 kW/kg LT-PEM or 20 kW/kg HT-PEM (2035), over 20 kW/kg (2050). Gaps named: hydrogen qualification of AM materials and joints from -253 C to 500 C, insufficient thin-wall property data, bespoke assembly tooling, automated NDT, multiscale flow modelling, transient thermo-mechanical life models, cryogenic and leak test rigs. HVM Catapult (MTC) listed as a contributor.

orgs.name: Department for Business, Energy and Industrial Strategy

thermal: Roadmap for hydrogen gas-turbine heat exchangers (fuel-oil, recuperator, cooled cooling air) and fuel-cell balance of plant (air radiator, precooler, hydrogen heater), with specific heat rejection targets.
manufacturing: Enablers: joining, assembly, automation, inspection and NDT, cost reduction, AM qualification in hydrogen, multiscale and transient modelling, cryogenic test facilities.

title: Thermal Management: UK Capability and Overseas Landscape (FZO-PPN-CAP-0067)
summary: FlyZero capability report: novel air radiator heat exchangers with a commercially attractive manufacturing method are 'a potential area of high opportunity for the UK'. Cryogenic hydrogen fluid heat exchangers are TRL 3 globally (no representative testing, limited materials data, sealing). UK gaps: cryogenic test facilities (UK firms test in the US), long thermal-cycling and hydrogen-exposure test facilities, modelling expertise. UK strengths: Oxford Thermofluids Institute, Meggitt, Reaction Engines, HS Marston, HiETA. Notes AM and automated laser welding under study at HVM Catapult and TWI, with qualification and lifing of printed heat exchangers in hydrogen still a challenge.
thermal: Fuel-cell air radiators, cryogenic hydrogen fluid heat exchangers, fuel-oil exchangers and recuperators.
manufacturing: AM for complex geometry and weight; automated laser welding; qualification and lifing of AM heat exchangers in hydrogen.

title: Oxford University to lead new collaboration advancing zero carbon aviation through hydrogen
publisher: Department of Engineering Science, University of Oxford
summary: £9.5M EPSRC programme launched June 2025 at the Oxford Thermofluids Institute to lay the scientific groundwork for cryogenic liquid hydrogen as a gas-turbine fuel, including heat transfer and thermal management of hydrogen fuel systems. Partners Imperial, Loughborough and King's College London; supporters include Rolls-Royce, Airbus, Honeywell, ZeroAvia, Boeing, Parker Hannifin and ESA. Over 12 studentships.
thermal: Cryogenic fluid flow, heat transfer and thermal management of hydrogen fuel systems.
manufacturing: New cryogenic hydrogen flow facilities and modelling; no manufacturing process.

title: Making Hydrogen Work in Zero Carbon Jet Engines
publisher: Oxford Thermofluids Institute, University of Oxford
summary: Project page for EPSRC EP/Z534456/1 (£9.5M). Questions: handling supercritical hydrogen, predicting pressure and heat transfer in cryogenic fuel lines, combustion instabilities from liquid-hydrogen injection, dominant materials failure mechanisms. Couples experiments and modelling to heat and pressurise liquid hydrogen from tank to combustor injection conditions.
thermal: Heating cryogenic hydrogen from tank to injection temperature; heat transfer in cryogenic fuel lines.
manufacturing: Modelling and experiment only; materials failure in hydrogen posed as a research question.

title: Pioneering thermal management solutions for hydrogen fuel-cell powered aircraft
summary: Project FRESSON (hydrogen-electric Britten-Norman Islander, passenger services targeted from 2027) adopted Reaction Engines' annular microtube radiator with mixed counter-crossflow, claimed to reject over 300 kW of low-grade fuel-cell waste heat with low weight and drag. Co-design with partners rather than fixed-spec tendering. Partners Evolito, Ricardo, Britten-Norman. No test data given. Reaction Engines entered administration in October 2024.
thermal: Annular microtube radiator, mixed counter-crossflow, over 300 kW low-grade fuel-cell heat (claim).
manufacturing: Microtube heat-exchanger construction (Reaction Engines IP); co-design approach.

title: Reaction Engines' hypersonic hopes stall as funding fizzles out
summary: Reaction Engines (Culham, Oxfordshire) entered administration on 31 October 2024 with PwC appointed; 173 of 208 staff made redundant. SABRE precooler tested in 2019. The article notes the precooler heat-exchanger technology is also used in F1 engine cooling. IP may be sold.
thermal: SABRE precooler: microtube heat exchanger cooling very hot intake air; spin-off use in F1 cooling.

title: Administrators Seek Buyer for Reaction Engines' Hypersonic Technology
summary: PwC administrators selling Reaction Engines' IP (patents, trade secrets), valued by directors at £848,000; a preferred bidder was in exclusivity as of June 2025. No technical results.
thermal: Passing mention of thermal-management technology developed alongside SABRE.
gate_reason: Context only: who now holds the UK microtube heat-exchanger IP.

title: Unlocking Advanced Heat Exchanger Design and Simulation with nTop Platform and ANSYS CFX
summary: Design workflow for an AM fuel-cooled oil cooler (FCOC) with a gyroid core: implicit modelling in nTop, CFD in ANSYS CFX. The FCOC cools engine oil and warms fuel to prevent ice crystals. Inspired by an America Makes project re-engineering a legacy component. Fetched excerpt has no CFD numbers.
thermal: Fuel-cooled oil cooler: engine oil to fuel.
manufacturing: Gyroid TPMS core designed for AM; implicit-modelling to CFD workflow.

title: Safran unveils HIPEX, its new heat exchanger for aircraft engines
summary: Safran Aero Boosters HIPEX: single-block, 3D-metal-printed curved air-oil heat exchangers that conform to the engine, claimed to halve aerodynamic drag at the same thermal performance and save up to 1% fuel on some engines. Tested on a Liège bench then on a civil engine in a ground campaign; no numbers released. Supported by the Walloon Region WINGS partnership.
thermal: Air-oil heat exchanger for engine oil cooling; half the drag at equal heat rejection (claim).
manufacturing: Single-block metal AM, curved or adjustable shape.

title: Thermal Management for the Hybrid Electric Regional Aircraft (TheMa4HERA)
summary: Clean Aviation project (2023-2026, €33.5M total, €25.4M EU), coordinated by Honeywell, to develop and test to TRL 5 on-board thermal management handling 300-1000 kW for hybrid-electric regional aircraft (today about 35-50 kW). Digital twin plus full-scale demonstrator at Fraunhofer IBP. UK partners (non-signatory): Conflux Technology UK, Reaction Engines, Honeywell UK, Element Digital Engineering. Others include Liebherr Toulouse, Collins Aerospace Ireland, Calyos, DLR, NLR, Fraunhofer, Airbus, ATR, Leonardo, ITP Aero.
thermal: Megawatt-class on-board thermal management: air cycle, vapour cycle, liquid loops, cabin air.
manufacturing: Digital twin and full-scale ground demonstrator; AM heat exchangers via Conflux.

title: Conflux Technology joins Honeywell-led consortium to advance hybrid-electric aircraft cooling systems
summary: Conflux joins TheMa4HERA (28 partners, 10 countries) to develop lightweight AM heat exchangers for air cycle (air-to-air) and vapour cycle (air-to-liquid evaporators and condensers) systems. Targets: 20-50 kW for systems, 300-1000 kW for batteries, APU and fuel cells; TRL 5 by 2026, flight testing in Clean Aviation Phase 2 from 2027.
thermal: AM air-to-air and air-to-liquid heat exchangers, evaporators and condensers.
manufacturing: Additive manufacture of lightweight heat exchangers; digital twins.

title: Conflux Advances Additive Manufacturing for Airbus's ZEROe Hydrogen Aircraft Program
summary: Conflux designed (CFD-led) an AM heat exchanger for Airbus ZEROe megawatt-class fuel-cell propulsion, 'confirmed by rigorous laboratory-scale trials'; now under technology readiness assessment and evaluation for Airbus's fuel-cell architecture. No data given.
thermal: Heat exchanger for megawatt-class hydrogen fuel-cell cooling.
manufacturing: AM heat exchanger designed with CFD.

title: Compact Additive Layer Manufactured Air Oil Heat Exchanger (C-ALM AOHE)
summary: Clean Sky 2 project (May 2019 to Oct 2022, €1.89M) coordinated by Meggitt Aerospace (UK) with TWI: design, build and test a compact AM air-oil heat exchanger for geared VHBR/UHBR turbofans. Targets: 80 kW heat load, dry weight 'significantly less than 10 kg', TRL 6, MRL 6. Thermal model validated by a thermally representative build. Closed; no results on the page.
thermal: Compact air-oil heat exchanger for UHBR oil cooling, 80 kW.
manufacturing: Additive layer manufacture of a novel-geometry core; thermal model validated by test.

title: Development of the Inclined Ducted Heat Exchanger System (DBAHX)
summary: ATI case study (£0.87M): Parker Meggitt inclined ducted heat exchanger system for UHBR, open-rotor and fuel-cell aircraft, aimed at lower drag. Flight-profile simulations validated in a full-scale custom wind tunnel built with a UK SME; compact inlet duct minimises separation. Validated design tools produced; AM ejector designed for off-design airflow; fire-proof composite ducts with NCC and AMRC. No numbers published.
thermal: Ducted air-oil heat exchanger installation; airflow and drag rather than heat-transfer results.
manufacturing: Simulation-led design, AM ejector, automated and hand composite layup.

title: Honeywell to Test Printed Heat Exchanger
summary: 2015: 3D Systems and Honeywell, $1.3M America Makes and AFRL contract with Penn State CIMP-3D, to test a DMP-printed fuel-oil heat exchanger for commercial aircraft. Old; background on how long AM fuel-oil heat exchangers have been in development.
thermal: Fuel-oil heat exchanger.
manufacturing: Direct metal printing of conformal heat exchangers.

title: GKN-backed Start-up Focuses on Electric Motors
summary: GKN Aerospace and the University of Nottingham form HP Drive Technologies to exploit H2Gear's cryogenically cooled 1 MW motor (99% efficiency claimed). H2Gear did not meet hydrogen tank permeability limits.
thermal: Cryogenic cooling mentioned; no thermal design detail.
gate_reason: Motor and investment news; the cryogenic cooling is mentioned but not described.

title: Additively manufactured parts testing underway for 2026 Ford and Red Bull F1 debut
summary: Ford has made around 1,000 AM parts for the 2026 Red Bull Ford power unit, including battery cold plates and cooling plates across the engine and hybrid system. Each part is checked for strength, hardness and 3D-scanned geometry, then X-rayed and CT scanned by Ford's NDE team before metrology. Ford plans to extend these quality controls to road cars. Company statements, no thermal data.
thermal: AM battery cold plates and cooling plates for the 2026 hybrid power unit.
manufacturing: Metal and polymer AM; strength, hardness, 3D scan, X-ray and CT inspection, then metrology.

title: Six things Honda's revealed about 2026 F1 engine
summary: Honda calls its 2026 power unit 'essentially a complete reset' with a much larger battery and control electronics. It names thermal management and temperature control of the battery and motor as areas where manufacturers will differ and that will affect reliability. No data.
thermal: Battery and motor thermal management named as a reliability differentiator.

title: Data center cooling tech startup Iceotope aims to scale after raising $26M
summary: Sheffield-based Iceotope closed a $26M Series B (Two Seas Capital, Barclays Climate Ventures) for product development of KUL AI racks and KUL BOX servers using non-flammable dielectric coolant. Cites SemiAnalysis: liquid-cooled AI accelerators growing from about 3 GW to over 40 GW in two years. Company claims only.
thermal: Dielectric precision liquid cooling for AI racks and servers.

title: £80m-backed Sheffield AI cooling company in two-horse race for UK's data centre deep freeze dominance
summary: Tracxn report: UK cooling and heat-reuse firms have raised about $362M, second only to the US, almost all in Deep Green ($255M Series D from Octopus Energy Generation) and Iceotope ($107M since 2013). It tracks 12 UK companies and names only one UK chip-level cooling company, Infiniflux. Globally over $2bn raised by 157 companies; $585M in 2026 so far versus $306M in all of 2024. Market data, not technical evidence.
thermal: Maps UK companies across facility cooling, rack liquid cooling, heat reuse and chip-level cooling.

title: Submer, Hammer partner to expand UK AI liquid cooling
summary: Submer signs UK distribution with Hammer for its liquid cooling products. Distribution news, no technical change.
thermal: Liquid and immersion cooling products; no detail.
gate_reason: Distribution deal with no technical content.

title: NATHENA: New Additive manufacTuring Heat ExchaNger for Aeronautic
summary: Clean Sky 2 project (2018-2022, €1.5M) with Liebherr Aerospace as topic manager: develop two optimised AM heat exchangers for civil aircraft with higher compactness and robustness, and a scale-1 proof-of-concept tested in the lab. Partners VKI (testing), AddUp (AM process), Sogeclair (mechanical design), Temisth (heat-exchanger design). AM reduces welded and brazed parts and allows a shape fitted to the aircraft. No results on the page.
thermal: Compact AM heat exchanger for aircraft air systems with a custom internal core.
manufacturing: AM core to cut welded and brazed joints; shape conformed to the installation.

title: LEAP 71 & Farsoon unveil 1.5-metre hypersonic precooler concept
summary: LEAP 71 (computational engineering, Dubai) and Farsoon printed a 1.5 m tall hypersonic precooler concept in one piece by L-PBF, designed by LEAP 71's Noyron model with a fractal folding algorithm to maximise surface area; liquid hydrogen cools superheated air. Shown at Formnext 2025. No thermal data.
thermal: Air-to-liquid-hydrogen precooler with fractal-folded surfaces.
manufacturing: Computationally generated geometry, single-piece large-format L-PBF.

title: Multi-circuit aerospace heat exchanger designed in 'record time'
summary: Sintavia designed, simulated and validated a multi-circuit aerospace heat exchanger in two weeks using GPU-accelerated conjugate heat transfer CFD (30M cells, 300 iterations in seven minutes, 11 times faster than CPU) with nTop implicit modelling. Claims 30% lower weight and 20% better thermal efficiency, validated by CT and in-house testing; no data published.
thermal: Multi-circuit heat exchanger designed with conjugate heat transfer CFD.
manufacturing: Implicit modelling, GPU CFD, AM build next day, CT inspection.

title: C-ALM AOHE: Improving Aircraft Heat Exchange Technology
summary: TWI announcement of its role with Meggitt in C-ALM AOHE: AM air-oil heat exchanger for geared VHBR/UHBR turbofans, 80 kW, under 10 kg, TRL 6 target.
thermal: Air-oil heat exchanger for UHBR oil cooling.
manufacturing: Additive layer manufacture, thermal model, build and test.

title: FIA and Formula E unveil GEN4: Setting a new benchmark for speed, sustainability and innovation in motorsport
summary: GEN4 Formula E car for 2026/27: 600 kW available, 450 kW race power, 700 kW regen, up to 55 kWh race energy, 50% more power than GEN3 Evo. Claims almost 100% motor efficiency. No thermal detail.
thermal: none
gate_reason: Powertrain figures only; no thermal content.

summary: Conflux developed an AM cartridge heat exchanger for the Pagani Utopia transmission oil system, claimed 30% more heat rejection than the previous design (no data). Pagani ran track, road and thermal shock trials. Conflux scaling production with an AUD 11M Series B.
